analyst.summary: Hindalco's FY26 PAT fell 16.3% even as revenue and EBITDA hit records, but the entire decline traces to a one-off, part-insured fire at Novelis's Oswego plant -- pre-exceptional Q4 PAT was actually a record, up 10% YoY, and India's aluminium-plus-copper business had its best year ever. The apparent '1-year growth acceleration' in the numbers is itself partly commodity-price pass-through (especially in copper) rather than pure volume growth, so neither the profit dip nor the revenue acceleration should be read at face value -- both are cycle/one-off noise cutting in opposite directions. The metals cycle is currently supportive for structural reasons (China's smelter cap, a new US copper tariff) that could fade within three years, but Hindalco also has real, funded capacity growth underway in both copper (400kt to 700kt) and aluminium (1.3mt to 1.7mt) that does not depend on prices holding. At roughly 16x trailing earnings for a business posting record core EBITDA, valuation is reasonable, not stretched -- supporting Hold on an existing position, not a reason to add or exit.
